question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 17 hours, pipe B can fill the same tank in 27 hours and pipe C can fill the same tank in 12 hours. The time taken by them to fill the same tank if they operate together is::
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total time to fill the tank together = 1 / (1/A + 1/B + 1/C)

Total time = 1 / (1/17 + 1/27 + 1/12)

Calculating the reciprocal of sum of efficiencies: 1836 / (108 + 68 + 153) = 1836 / 329

1836 ÷ 329 = 5(191/329) hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 5(191)/(329) hr.**

⇒ **Total Work** (LCM of 17, 27, 12) = 17 × 27 × 4 = 1836 units.

⇒ **Efficiency** of A = 1836 ÷ 17 = 108 units/hr.

⇒ **Efficiency** of B = 1836 ÷ 27 = 68 units/hr.

⇒ **Efficiency** of C = 1836 ÷ 12 = 153 units/hr.

⇒ Combined Efficiency = 108 + 68 + 153 = 329 units/hr.

⇒ Time taken = 1836 ÷ 329 = 5(191/329) hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 5(191)/(329) hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Basics

Efficiency of an inlet pipe is positive, whereas efficiency of an outlet (leak) pipe is considered negative. Total work = Time × Efficiency.

Combined Work Formula

If pipe A fills in x hours and pipe B fills in y hours, they together fill in (xy)/(x + y) hours.</p
